beats.label: S1 · The man with two lives
beats.text: Ad man Don Draper closes a Lucky Strike pitch in Manhattan, then rides a train home to a wife and two kids nobody at the office knows exist.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the central deception that every future season pressures.

beats.label: S1 · Pete gets a secret
beats.text: Junior man Pete Campbell sleeps with new secretary Peggy Olson the night before his wedding, planting a bond that outlasts his marriage.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Seeds the Pete–Peggy child that pays off in the finale.

beats.label: S1 · Brother at the door
beats.text: A stranger named Adam Whitman recognises Don as his lost brother Dick; Don pays him $5,000 to vanish and never contact him again.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the Dick Whitman identity and the guilt that drives Don's later collapses.

beats.label: S1 · Pete opens the box
beats.text: A package from Adam is misdelivered to Pete, who finds proof Don is really Dick Whitman and tries to blackmail him into a promotion.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First person inside the office to hold Don's secret.

beats.label: S1 · Bert shrugs it off
beats.text: Don promotes the outsider Duck Phillips over Pete as head of accounts; Pete retaliates by telling senior partner Bert Cooper that Don is an impostor, but Bert waves it away.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Shows the secret is survivable inside the firm and sets up Duck as a rival.

beats.label: S1 · Peggy has a baby
beats.text: Peggy, promoted to junior copywriter, goes to hospital with stomach pains and delivers Pete's child, then refuses to acknowledge the boy.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The hidden pregnancy is the season's biggest unresolved fact.

beats.label: S1 · Empty house at Thanksgiving
beats.text: Don wins Kodak with a nostalgia pitch about family, calls home imagining Betty and the kids waiting, and walks into a dark, empty house.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the season with Don's professional peak set against his private hollowness.

cliffhanger.text: Don's Kodak triumph is undercut by a house standing empty for Thanksgiving. Adam has hanged himself, Peggy has secretly given birth to Pete's son, and Pete now knows Don was once someone called Dick Whitman.
questions: Will Pete use what he found in Adam's box now that Bert has dismissed it?
Can Don's marriage survive Betty's growing suspicion of the man she lives with?
What happens to the baby Peggy refuses to name?

characters.name: Don Draper
characters.line: Star creative at Sterling Cooper, secretly a Korean War deserter named Dick Whitman living a stolen identity.

characters.name: Betty Draper
characters.line: Don's suburban wife in Ossining, in therapy for anxiety and quietly beginning to sense his lies.

characters.name: Peggy Olson
characters.line: Don's ex-secretary just promoted to junior copywriter, and the unacknowledged mother of Pete's newborn son.

characters.name: Pete Campbell
characters.line: Ambitious junior accounts man, freshly married to Trudy, who knows Don was born Dick Whitman.

characters.name: Roger Sterling
characters.line: Senior partner recovering from a heart attack, Don's protector and drinking companion.

characters.name: Bert Cooper
characters.line: The firm's eccentric owner, who has chosen to protect Don's secret rather than act on it.

characters.name: Joan Holloway
characters.line: Office manager and Roger's on-and-off mistress, the unofficial power over every woman on the floor.

characters.name: Salvatore Romano
characters.line: Art director, closeted, who turned down a hotel invitation, too afraid to follow through on his attraction to men.

beats.label: S2 · A marriage already cracking
beats.text: It is Valentine's Day 1962; Don cannot perform with Betty, and Peggy returns from a three-month absence nobody in the office can quite explain.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reopens the two hidden wounds carried out of season 1.

beats.label: S2 · Duck sells the firm out
beats.text: To land American Airlines, accounts head Duck Phillips forces Don to drop Mohawk and, when denied a partnership, secretly offers Sterling Cooper to his old London firm PPL.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The mechanism that puts the firm up for sale and sets up Don's power play in S3.

beats.label: S2 · Bobbie and the crash
beats.text: Don's affair with the wife of client Jimmy Barrett ends in a drunk car crash; Peggy bails him out, and Jimmy later tells Betty about the affair.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The specific infidelity that finally gives Betty proof.

beats.label: S2 · Betty throws him out
beats.text: After a humiliating dinner party, Betty confirms the affair and phones Don at the office to tell him not to come home.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The separation is the emotional axis of the back half.

beats.label: S2 · Don vanishes to California
beats.text: Sent west on business, Don abandons the convention, drifts with wealthy nomads, and visits Anna Draper — the widow of the real Don Draper, who knows exactly who he is.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Anna and reframes the stolen identity as something a woman has willingly kept.

beats.label: S2 · The firm is sold
beats.text: With Don unreachable, Roger and Bert accept PPL's buyout of Sterling Cooper; Duck expects to be installed as its new head.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The ownership change that drives every S3 political move.

beats.label: S2 · No contract, no leverage
beats.text: Don returns, faces down Duck, and reveals he never signed a contract, killing Duck's coup. Betty asks him home and tells him she is pregnant.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Duck loses, Don is unbound, and a third Draper child is on the way — all in the same beat.

beats.label: S2 · Peggy tells Pete the truth
beats.text: During the Cuban Missile Crisis, Pete confesses he loves her; Peggy answers that she had his baby and gave it away, then walks out.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Detonates the season 1 pregnancy and reshapes Pete forever.

cliffhanger.text: Sterling Cooper has been sold to PPL, Duck's coup has failed, and Don has walked back into a marriage that now includes a baby conceived on the eve of separation. Peggy has finally told Pete he fathered her child.
questions: What kind of firm will Sterling Cooper be under British owners?
Can Don and Betty's reconciliation survive a pregnancy neither of them planned?
How does Pete carry the knowledge that he has a son somewhere he will never meet?

characters.name: Don Draper
characters.line: Back in his marriage after a separation, unbound by any contract at the newly-sold firm.

characters.name: Betty Draper
characters.line: Pregnant with a third child, tentatively reconciled with Don after briefly throwing him out.

characters.name: Peggy Olson
characters.line: Now a copywriter with her own office, and no longer carrying the child-with-Pete secret alone.

characters.name: Pete Campbell
characters.line: Just told he has a son by Peggy; struggling to conceive with Trudy and hungry for status at the merged firm.

characters.name: Roger Sterling
characters.line: Has left his wife Mona for Don's young ex-secretary Jane and sold the firm to PPL.

characters.name: Joan Holloway
characters.line: Engaged to Dr. Greg Harris, who raped her on the floor of Don's office; she has told no one.

characters.name: Duck Phillips
characters.line: The accounts man who engineered the PPL sale to install himself as president — and just lost the fight for it.

characters.name: Bert Cooper
characters.line: Senior partner who signed off on the PPL sale, now a passenger at his own firm.

characters.name: Anna Draper
characters.line: The widow of the real Don Draper, living in California, the one person who knows and forgives Dick Whitman.

beats.label: S3 · The British move in
beats.text: PPL installs Lane Pryce as financial officer; he pits Pete and Ken against each other as co-heads of accounts, keeping both hungry and neither secure.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Lane and the political geometry the whole season runs on.

beats.label: S3 · Don meets Connie
beats.text: At a Kentucky Derby party Don befriends a folksy stranger who turns out to be hotelier Conrad Hilton and later demands Don sign a three-year contract.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Hilton account is the lever Bert uses to finally chain Don down.

beats.label: S3 · Bert breaks Don
beats.text: Bert reveals he knows Don was Dick Whitman and forces him to sign the three-year Sterling Cooper contract to keep Hilton — the secret is now a leash.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Season 1's secret is finally cashed in against Don.

beats.label: S3 · Betty finds the drawer
beats.text: Betty picks Don's locked desk, finds photos, a divorce decree from Anna and the deed to Anna's house, and forces Don to tell her his entire hidden life.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the marriage in every way except paperwork.

beats.label: S3 · Kennedy and Henry Francis
beats.text: JFK is shot; while Don stays composed, Betty runs to political aide Henry Francis, who proposes marriage. She comes home and tells Don she no longer loves him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Betty's exit is decided; Henry is the man she will leave for.

beats.label: S3 · Sterling Cooper Draper Pryce
beats.text: Learning McCann is buying the firm, Don, Roger, Bert and Lane stage a weekend coup and poach Peggy, Pete, Joan and Harry to launch a new agency: SCDP.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The single most important structural event in the series — the firm the rest of the show lives inside.

beats.label: S3 · Don moves out
beats.text: Betty threatens to expose the Dick Whitman identity if Don blocks the divorce; Don consents, and Betty flies to Reno with Henry and baby Gene.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Leaves Don a bachelor and Betty already partnered as season 4 opens.

cliffhanger.text: A brand new firm — Sterling Cooper Draper Pryce — has been born in a hotel suite, staffed by defectors and no clients guaranteed. Don has lost his marriage, and Betty is already on a plane to Reno with Henry Francis.
questions: Can a firm assembled in a weekend keep the clients it walked out with?
What kind of father is Don when he no longer lives with his children?
Who at the old Sterling Cooper — Sal, Kinsey, Ken — makes it into the new firm's future?

characters.name: Don Draper
characters.line: Founding partner of SCDP, newly separated from Betty, contractually chained after Bert wielded the Dick Whitman file.

characters.name: Betty Draper
characters.line: Flying to Reno for a divorce with Henry Francis and baby Gene; the family house in Ossining is behind her.

characters.name: Roger Sterling
characters.line: Co-founded SCDP with Don; married to Jane and increasingly a bystander at his own firm.

characters.name: Bert Cooper
characters.line: Co-founder of SCDP, the man who used Don's Dick Whitman secret to force his loyalty.

characters.name: Lane Pryce
characters.line: British financial officer who quietly fired Sterling Cooper for Don and Roger and became the fourth name on the door.

characters.name: Pete Campbell
characters.line: One of the four staffers Don personally poached for the new firm.

characters.name: Peggy Olson
characters.line: Brought to SCDP after Don, for the first time, openly named her as indispensable.

characters.name: Joan Harris
characters.line: Left Sterling Cooper for retail, then recruited back to run the new agency's floor while Greg trains as an Army surgeon.

characters.name: Henry Francis
characters.line: Political aide to the Rockefeller camp, engaged to Betty and about to raise Don's children.

characters.name: Conrad Hilton
characters.line: Hotelier client whose contract demand gave Bert the leverage to bind Don to Sterling Cooper.

beats.label: S4 · Who is Don Draper?
beats.text: SCDP is a year old and scrapping; a bad Ad Age profile and a lost client push Don to give a defiant Wall Street Journal interview about walking out of the old firm.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the season's identity question and puts SCDP on the map.

beats.label: S4 · Anna dies
beats.text: Don visits Anna in California and learns she has terminal cancer; her death, later relayed by phone, breaks him open during an all-nighter with Peggy on Samsonite.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The one person who knew Dick Whitman is gone; the Don–Peggy partnership deepens into its adult form.

beats.label: S4 · Lucky Strike walks
beats.text: Lee Garner Jr. tells Roger that Lucky Strike — a third of the firm's billings — is leaving for BBDO. Roger hides the loss and fakes a rescue trip.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The financial catastrophe that drives every desperate act to follow.

beats.label: S4 · Joan's decision
beats.text: Joan learns she is pregnant by Roger during a mugging-night encounter, sets up an abortion but ultimately keeps the baby, telling Greg it is his.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kevin's true parentage becomes a permanent private fact between Joan and Roger.

beats.label: S4 · Don burns the tobacco bridge
beats.text: After Philip Morris cancels, Don prints a full-page ad in the New York Times swearing SCDP will no longer take tobacco business; Bert quits in protest.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Defines Don's public reputation and costs the firm a founder.

beats.label: S4 · Megan in California
beats.text: On a business trip Don brings his secretary Megan Calvet to mind the kids; impressed by her ease with them, he proposes with Anna's ring and ends his relationship with Faye Miller.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The engagement that reshapes both Don's home life and the firm.

beats.label: S4 · The firm on a pantyhose
beats.text: Peggy and Ken sign Topaz Pantyhose, keeping SCDP alive for another quarter, as Betty fires the maid and Henry accuses her of pushing everyone away.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The firm survives, but only just; Betty's new home is already fraying.

cliffhanger.text: SCDP has clawed itself back from Lucky Strike's exit with a pantyhose account, and Don has stunned the office by announcing he is marrying his secretary Megan instead of the woman everyone expected. Faye is out, Bert has quit, and Joan is quietly carrying Roger's child as her husband ships out.
questions: Can a firm running on a pantyhose account actually survive the year ahead?
Is Megan the new life Don thinks she is, or the next mistake?
How long can Joan keep Kevin's true father a secret from Roger, from Greg, and from herself?

characters.name: Don Draper
characters.line: Newly engaged to Megan; his one confidante, Anna, is dead, and his anti-tobacco letter has redefined him in the industry.

characters.name: Megan Calvet
characters.line: Don's secretary and now fiancée, aspiring actress, wearing the engagement ring Anna once wore.

characters.name: Betty Francis
characters.line: Living in Rye with Henry, freshly rid of the maid Carla, and drifting from both her husband and her children.

characters.name: Peggy Olson
characters.line: Copy chief in all but name, closer to Don than ever, dating underground journalist Abe Drexler.

characters.name: Joan Harris
characters.line: Pregnant with Roger's child but passing it off as Greg's while he serves in Vietnam.

characters.name: Roger Sterling
characters.line: Losing power at SCDP after Lucky Strike walked out; the unacknowledged father of Joan's baby.

characters.name: Pete Campbell
characters.line: The rainmaker holding the firm together account by account; a new father to daughter Tammy.

characters.name: Lane Pryce
characters.line: Estranged from his wife, quietly living in New York and running SCDP's books.

characters.name: Faye Miller
characters.line: Consumer psychologist Don was dating openly — dropped the moment Megan said yes.

characters.name: Dr. Faye's replacement (Sally Draper)
characters.line: Don and Betty's eldest, now in therapy with Dr. Edna, increasingly the moral witness of both households.

beats.label: S5 · Marriage on display
beats.text: It is 1966; Megan throws Don a surprise 40th birthday party and performs 'Zou Bisou Bisou'. Don is furious, and the office spends weeks unpacking what her presence there means.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets Megan inside the firm and inside the marriage as an unstable object.

beats.label: S5 · Megan quits
beats.text: Promoted to copywriter, Megan realises she wants to act; with Don's blessing she quits SCDP, and he immediately resents having agreed.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reshapes the Draper marriage into the shape it will carry into S6.

beats.label: S5 · Joan and Jaguar
beats.text: To land Jaguar, the partners privately agree to offer Joan up to Herb Rennet for a night; Joan sleeps with him in exchange for a 5% partnership stake.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Joan is now a partner; the price sits between her and Don for good.

beats.label: S5 · Peggy leaves
beats.text: Unappreciated and worn out, Peggy accepts a chief copywriter job at Ted Chaough's CGC; Don kisses her hand and lets her go.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Splits the show's central creative partnership and plants Peggy at the rival that will later merge in.

beats.label: S5 · Lane's forged check
beats.text: Squeezed by British tax debt, Lane forges Don's signature on a $7,500 cheque. When Don discovers it he fires Lane, who hangs himself in his office.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes a founding partner and leaves Don carrying the guilt into every subsequent season.

beats.label: S5 · Sally grows up early
beats.text: Sally is caught in a Peter-and-the-wolf triangle with schoolboy Glen and stepgrandmother Pauline; while at Don's apartment she gets her first period and flees home to Betty.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Marks Sally's transition into the show's moral witness of Don.

beats.label: S5 · Are you alone?
beats.text: Megan lands a commercial through the agency; watching her on set, Don walks off, sits at a bar and is asked by a woman if he's alone. He does not answer.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends Don's fidelity experiment on an ambiguous, open shot.

cliffhanger.text: Lane is dead, Peggy is gone to CGC, Joan is a partner at a cost she and Don both know, and Megan is now a paid actress via a favour Don couldn't help himself from doing. Don walks away from her set alone, into a bar, into a familiar question.
questions: Does Don break his marriage the same way he broke his last one?
Can SCDP hold together after losing Lane and Peggy in the same summer?
What is Joan when everyone in the room now knows how she got her partnership?

characters.name: Don Draper
characters.line: Newly a partner in a rich firm, married a year and already turning toward the bar; carrying Lane's suicide privately.

characters.name: Megan Draper
characters.line: Don's wife, no longer a copywriter, starting an acting career with a commercial her husband arranged.

characters.name: Peggy Olson
characters.line: Chief copywriter at rival agency Cutler Gleason Chaough after Don failed to promote or acknowledge her.

characters.name: Joan Harris
characters.line: Newly divorced from Greg, a 5% partner in SCDP after sleeping with a Jaguar client at the partners' urging.

characters.name: Roger Sterling
characters.line: The father of Joan's son Kevin, freshly separated from Jane after a shared LSD trip, still a partner in name.

characters.name: Pete Campbell
characters.line: Increasingly bitter suburban commuter chasing affairs; the account man who actually keeps the firm fed.

characters.name: Sally Draper
characters.line: A teenager now, moving between Betty and Don's households, awake to both parents' failures.

characters.name: Betty Francis
characters.line: Living in Rye with Henry; a recent cancer scare turned out to be benign but has left her rattled.

characters.name: Ted Chaough
characters.line: Creative director at CGC — Peggy's new boss and Don's declared professional rival.

beats.label: S6 · Don is cheating again
beats.text: Hawaii sun; Don is having an affair with Sylvia Rosen, wife of his neighbour, surgeon Arnold Rosen. The Hershey ad brief will circle back at year's end.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the private betrayal that Sally will uncover.

beats.label: S6 · The merger
beats.text: About to lose both Chevy and Vicks in one week, Don and Ted meet in a Detroit bar and merge SCDP with CGC to fake the size Chevy demanded; Peggy is named copy chief.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Rebuilds the firm as SC&P — the vehicle that carries the show to the end.

beats.label: S6 · Sally opens the door
beats.text: Sally walks in on Don with Sylvia; Don tries to explain, but the trust between them is broken from that moment on.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The most consequential single event of Don's private life all season.

beats.label: S6 · Bob Benson's cover
beats.text: Pete discovers junior man Bob Benson is a fraud with a fake résumé and a manservant's past; he keeps the secret for leverage rather than exposing him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Bob is season 6's echo of Don, and Pete now holds a card.

beats.label: S6 · The Hershey confession
beats.text: In a pitch to Hershey, Don abandons the script and tells the executives he grew up in a brothel where Hershey bars were his only comfort.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The public unmasking that finally cracks Don's professional standing.

beats.label: S6 · Don is put on leave
beats.text: The partners place Don on indefinite leave and name Lou Avery acting creative head; Ted flees to run the California office as Megan tells Don she is leaving him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Don from the firm and from the marriage in one stroke.

beats.label: S6 · Show them where you're from
beats.text: On Thanksgiving Don drives Sally, Bobby and Gene to the derelict brothel where he grew up. Sally looks at him differently for the first time.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First step in Don's late-series attempt to be known instead of hidden.

cliffhanger.text: SC&P is a real firm with a real Chevy account, but Don has been suspended from the agency he founded and separated from his wife after telling clients the truth about the brothel. Sally has caught him mid-affair; Pete is quietly holding blackmail on Bob Benson.
questions: Does Don ever get back into SC&P, and on whose terms?
Can Sally look at her father again?
How long can Bob Benson keep his invented life if Pete decides to talk?

characters.name: Don Draper
characters.line: On indefinite leave from SC&P after confessing his brothel childhood to a client; his marriage to Megan is effectively over.

characters.name: Megan Draper
characters.line: A working soap actress in New York; she has told Don she is leaving for California without him.

characters.name: Sally Draper
characters.line: A teenager at boarding school who has caught her father in bed with a neighbour's wife and is no longer his ally.

characters.name: Peggy Olson
characters.line: Copy chief of the merged SC&P, dating and then separated from Ted, working under both her old boss and her old boyfriend.

characters.name: Ted Chaough
characters.line: Partner at SC&P after the merger; slept with Peggy and has fled to run the California office to escape her.

characters.name: Pete Campbell
characters.line: His mother has vanished (apparently married and killed by con-man 'Manolo'), and he has moved to Los Angeles after losing Chevy.

characters.name: Bob Benson
characters.line: Rising accounts man whose entire résumé is invented; Pete knows and hasn't told anyone.

characters.name: Jim Cutler
characters.line: New senior partner from the CGC side; running SC&P as a cost-cutter in Don's absence.

characters.name: Roger Sterling
characters.line: Still a partner.

characters.name: Joan Harris
characters.line: Partner increasingly leading her own accounts, quietly raising Roger's son Kevin.

beats.label: S7 · Back on probation
beats.text: Don is reinstated as a copywriter under new creative head Lou Avery on humiliating written conditions; he bides his time feeding ideas through Freddy Rumsen.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Frames the entire first half — Don rebuilding his position from below.

beats.label: S7 · Bert dies, McCann buys
beats.text: Neil Armstrong walks on the moon; Bert Cooper dies in his sleep, and Roger secretly sells 51% of SC&P to McCann Erickson to keep it as an independent subsidiary.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Loses the last founding-era steward and sets up the buyout that ends the firm.

beats.label: S7 · Peggy wins Burger Chef
beats.text: With Don's future in doubt he hands Peggy the Burger Chef pitch; she lands it and, at long last, is publicly the equal he made her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Peggy's ceiling breaks; sets up her McCann move.

beats.label: S7 · McCann swallows SC&P
beats.text: Jim Hobart tells the partners that SC&P is being fully absorbed into McCann; Don's proposal to spin off a west-coast satellite is refused.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The firm ceases to exist; everyone chooses whether to go with it.

beats.label: S7 · The women exit McCann
beats.text: Harassed at McCann, Joan takes a half-value buyout and walks; Peggy stays and, in an empty SC&P, roller-skates through the office with Roger before starting.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Splits the two women who defined the firm into different futures.

beats.label: S7 · Betty is dying
beats.text: Betty is diagnosed with terminal lung cancer and refuses treatment; she writes Sally instructions for her burial and asks that the children go to her brother's family, not Don.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The last major shock of the series and the reason Don is out of options at home.

beats.label: S7 · Don gives it all away
beats.text: Don drives west, hits a veterans' hall in Oklahoma, confesses to killing his C.O. in Korea, gives his car away to a young thief and waits for a bus with nothing.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the finale's California retreat as a shed-everything endpoint.

beats.label: S7 · Hilltop
beats.text: Don, ruined, calls Peggy from a California retreat; in a group meditation he embraces a stranger, smiles, and the ad for Coca-Cola's 'Hilltop' plays.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The series' final image — Don's breakdown reframed as the ad that made him money.

cliffhanger.text: Mad Men ends. SC&P has been absorbed into McCann. Betty is dying and Sally is going home to look after Bobby and Gene. Peggy is with Stan, Joan is running her own production company, Pete has left for Wichita with Trudy, and Don — stripped of car, wife and firm — sits on a Californian hillside, smiles, and the Coke ad plays.
questions: Did Don write the Coke ad, or is the ad simply what a man like him becomes?
What kind of life do Sally, Bobby and Gene inherit once Betty is gone?
Is there anything left of the people the show began with, or only the work they made?

characters.name: Don Draper
characters.line: The series ends with him at a California retreat, having shed his firm, his marriage and his car, smiling at the Coke ad his life has become.

characters.name: Peggy Olson
characters.line: A senior copywriter at McCann who has finally told Stan she loves him.

characters.name: Joan Holloway
characters.line: Bought out of McCann for half her stake; founding her own production company after Ken hires her to produce a Dow film.

characters.name: Roger Sterling
characters.line: Marrying Megan's mother Marie and quietly leaving his fortune to his and Joan's son Kevin.

characters.name: Pete Campbell
characters.line: Reunited with Trudy and moving to Wichita for a job with Learjet.

characters.name: Betty Francis
characters.line: Terminally ill with lung cancer, having refused treatment and arranged for her children to live with her brother.

characters.name: Sally Draper
characters.line: Home from school to look after Bobby and Gene as her mother dies.

characters.name: Ted Chaough
characters.line: Back in New York and back with SC&P's absorbed leadership at McCann after his California collapse.
